details.description: GLM-5.2 is Z.ai's (formerly Zhipu AI) open-weight Mixture-of-Experts flagship model, released June 16, 2026, offered on Together AI. It has 753 billion parameters and a 1,048,576-token (1M) context window, per its Hugging Face model card, and uses an IndexShare sparse-attention design that Z.ai says reuses the same indexer across every four sparse-attention layers to cut per-token compute by 2.9x at a 1M context length. It supports thinking modes, function calling, streaming, structured JSON output, and MCP tool integration, and Z.ai positions it for large-scale codebase comprehension, multi-file refactoring, and long-horizon agentic engineering. It is released under the MIT license. Z.ai has since released GLM-5.3 (August 18, 2026), a newer generation.
advantages: Scores 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro and 91.2 on GPQA-Diamond, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 99.2 on AIME 2026 and 81.0 on Terminal Bench 2.1 (Terminus-2), per its Hugging Face model card.
1,048,576-token (1M) context window, using an IndexShare architecture Z.ai says reduces per-token compute at long context lengths, per its Hugging Face model card.
Released under the permissive MIT license.
Scores higher than GLM-5.1 on every benchmark Z.ai lists for both models, including SWE-bench Pro (62.1 vs. 58.4) and AIME 2026 (99.2 vs. 95.3), per its Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: Superseded as Z.ai's flagship by GLM-5.3, released August 18, 2026, per Z.ai's release notes and GitHub repository.
Text-only model; Z.ai's documentation describes no image or audio input support.
Z.ai's model card documents support for English and Chinese only.
use_cases: Large-scale codebase comprehension and multi-file refactoring
Long-horizon agentic engineering and terminal-based operations

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (1,048,575) and max_output_tokens (128,000) closely match the Hugging Face card's 1,048,576-token context window and Z.ai's stated 128K max output; kept the catalog's exact figures per instructions. This entry is Together AI's listing of the same underlying model already covered under sibling slugs for Fireworks AI and Mistral AI; those sibling entries carry host-specific deprecation notices (e.g. Fireworks' serverless cutoff) that do not apply here and are not in this target's catalog facts, so this entry states only the model's own supersession by GLM-5.3.
